### Load Calibration

For this modeling exercise, we use the most recent version of IntCal or
IntCal20. Note that we convert means and errors to fraction modern (`f14c_mu`
and `f14c_sigma`) since it is more reliable for older samples that may have
asymmetric uncertainty around the mean.

```{r}
#| label: intcal20

intcal20 <- structure(
  read.csv("data/intcal20.csv"),
  class = c("Calibration", "data.frame"),
  curve = "IntCal20"
)

intcal20 <- intcal20 |>
  transform(f14c_mu = exp(-c14_age / LIBBY)) |>
  transform(f14c_sigma = f14c_mu * c14_error / LIBBY)

intcal20
```

### Simulate Chronology

To simulate a chronology over the interval $[t_{min}, t_{max}]$, we randomly
sample the mixture parameters $\theta = \{w_{k}, \mu_{k}, \sigma_{k}\}$ for
$k = 1, ..., K$ components

$$
\begin{aligned}
w_{k} &\sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\mathbf{1}_{K})\\
\mu_{k} &\sim \mathrm{DiscreteUniform}(B_{k}) \\
\sigma_{k} &\sim \mathrm{Gamma}(4, 4/\lambda)
\end{aligned}
$$

where $B_{k}$ is the $k$th of $K$ equally spaced bins partitioning
$[t_{min}, t_{max}]$ and $\lambda = (t_{max} - t_{min})/20$ is the mean of the
component errors, scaling them with the length of the interval. We then
evaluate the mixture over the
annual grid $t_{j} = t_{min}, ..., t_{max}$ and normalize, in effect generating
a truncated and discrete empirical distribution

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bar{\mathbf{v}}_{j} &= \sum_{k} w_{k} \hspace{2pt} f(t_{j} \mid \mu_{k}, \sigma_{k}) \\
\mathrm{v}_{j} &= \frac{\bar{\mathrm{v}}_{j}}{\sum_{j} \bar{\mathbf{v}}_{j}}
\end{aligned}
$$

with $f$ a Gaussian, uniform, or randomly reflected Gamma density parameterized
by its mean and standard deviation.

```{r}
#| label: function-simulate-chronology
#| file: R/simulate-chronology.R
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: R/simulate-chronology.R
#| eval: false
```

Example:

```{r}
#| label: example-chronology
set.seed(STARTREK)

chronology <- simulate_chronology(500, 3500, 5)
chronology
```

### Sample Dates

Following the generative model outlined above and in the main text, we sample
years from $\mathbf{v}$ using inverse transform sampling.

$$
t_{1}, ..., t_{n} \sim p(t \mid \theta) \approx \mathrm{Categorical}(\mathbf{v})
$$

The years are the categories in this case, and $\mathbf{v}$ gives the 
probability of drawing each one. So, once we have those sample years, we then 
pass them to the calibration curve model and have it predict fraction modern 
measurements for those years.

$$
\mu(t_{i}) \mid t_{i} \sim N(m(t_{i}), s(t_{i})^{2})
$$

Finally, we add randomly sampled measurement uncertainty $z_{i}$.

$$
F_{i} \mid \mu(t_{i}) \sim N(\mu(t_{i}), z_{i}^{2})
$$

In R:

```r
# sample years using R's binary search (which is competitive with Rust!)
cdf <- cumsum(v)
j <- findInterval(runif(n), cdf, all.inside = TRUE)
t <- years[j]

# this is equivalent to
t <- sample(years, size = n, replace = TRUE, prob = v)

# add calibration uncertainty
xcalcurve <- rnorm(n, mean = mt, sd = st^2)

# add measurement uncertainty
Fi <- rnorm(n, mean = xcalcurve, sd = zi^2)
```

This and the above `simulate_chronology()` function are based on
`CreateDataVaryWeight()` used in (Heaton 2021, [github link](https://github.com/TJHeaton/NonparametricCalibration/blob/main/SimStudyFuncsFinal.R)).

```{r}
#| label: function-sample-dates
#| file: R/sample-dates.R
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: R/sample-dates.R
#| eval: false
```

Example:

```{r}
#| label: example-sample
set.seed(STARGATE)

samples <- sample_dates(chronology, 25, intcal20)
samples
```

### Calibrate Samples

Most of the algorithms outlined below rely on the calibrated dates as the main
data for modeling. These are stored in an $n \times m$ measurement matrix
$\mathbf{M}$ with $n$ samples evaluated over $m$ years.

$$
\mathrm{M}_{ij} \approx p(F_{i} \mid t_{j}) = N(F_{i} \mid m(t_{j}), s(t_{j})^{2} + z_{i}^{2})
$$

```r
# for an individual sample Fi
# with mt and st being length-m vectors supplied by the calibration curve
Mi <- dnorm(Fi, mean = mt, sd = sqrt(st^2 + z^2))
```

```{r}
#| label: function-calibrate
#| file: R/calibrate.R
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: R/calibrate.R
#| eval: false
```

```{r}
#| label: calibrate-dates
calibrated_dates <- calibrate(samples, intcal20)
calibrated_dates
```
